title: Compact NVTX naming and stream-linked kernel metrics for low-cardinality runtime traces
creator: Arielle Koh
description: Introduce a low-cardinality NVTX and span naming convention and attach CUDA stream-linked trace IDs so we can attribute per-kernel latency/CPU/GPU metrics back to user requests with minimal cardinality and overhead. Current NVTX labels are too verbose and high-cardinality (full op names + param suffixes) which floods exporters and makes aggregation expensive. This ticket designs and implements: 1) a compact canonical naming scheme mapping kernels to op families, batching mode, and quantization/precision; 2) propagation of a lightweight trace token onto CUDA streams so exemplar & span linking is possible for sampled requests; 3) a sampling strategy and reservoir to bound NVTX overhead for large requests; 4) exporter-side labels and histogram buckets for per-kernel latency, with exemplar trace IDs for p98/p99 latencies.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by runtime and telemetry leads (link above)
Runtime emits NVTX ranges using the new compact naming scheme in prefill and decode hot paths on all supported platforms (CUDA 11/12)
CUDA stream user-data carries a 64-bit trace token that can be used as Prometheus/Datadog exemplar and in Tempo/Jaeger spans
End-to-end test verifies that a sampled request produces a top-level trace that contains kernel spans and that exemplar IDs appear on p95/p99 histogram buckets
Telemetry overhead validated: CPU + NVTX instrumentation does not add >2% tail latency on our decode microbenchmarks at 95th percentile
Rollout plan and feature flag exist to enable/disable full NVTX naming per deployment tier (hosted/dedicated/private).
tasks: Finalize compact NVTX name spec (format: rt:kernel:{family}:{short_kernel}:{mode}) and publish to Confluence
Implement mapping table from detailed kernel identifiers to canonical families in runtime (C++/Rust module)
Add CUDA stream trace token API: attach/clear token, thread-safe, small memory, zero-copy where possible
Emit Prometheus histograms and gauges for kernel_latency_ms with labels: kernel_family, precision, batching_mode, model_shard; attach exemplar(trace_token) for high buckets
Implement reservoir sampling policy for NVTX/Span emission on multi-request batches and large seq lengths to control cardinality
Add unit + integration tests (simulated kernels) and a microbenchmark to measure instrumentation overhead
Create rollout PR, feature-flag gating and canary plan for hosted and dedicated clusters
notes: Trade-offs considered: (1) full NVTX names give best debug info but explode cardinality; compact families preserve signal while enabling long-term aggregation. (2) Storing trace tokens on CUDA streams couples runtime and tracing; mitigated by small 64-bit tokens and explicit clear calls to avoid leak across requests. (3) Sampling requires deterministic rules so high-QoS customers can opt into full traces via config.
implementation_plan: Phase A: Spec + small PoC that emits compact NVTX ranges for decode path and attaches trace token to stream. Phase B: Expand to prefill, implement exporter exemplar, attempt integrated end-to-end traces on devcluster. Phase C: Performance validation, rollback hooks and staged rollout across regions.
observability_runbook: If kernel_p99 spikes after rollout: 1) toggle feature-flag to disable NVTX exemplar emission; 2) compare histograms by kernel_family; 3) use canary traces to identify misattributed long-running kernels; 4) rollback to previous runtime if necessary.
review_feedback: PM: prioritize low cardinality to avoid billing/ingestion spikes
SRE: require explicit feature flag and quota for exemplar exports in hosted clusters
Perf: ensure sampling reservoir is O(1) per-request and thread-safe
